title: Medial Elbow Tendinopathy (Golfer's Elbow)
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Inner elbow pain with gripping, wrist flexion and forearm pronation (turning the palm down). Tenderness just in front of and below the medial epicondyle.
qa: Why check the ulnar nerve? It lies close to the medial epicondyle and is often irritated alongside.
Which test helps detect UCL injury in throwers? Moving valgus stress test.
What is the core treatment? Progressive tendon loading.
Child pitcher with medial elbow pain? Consider apophysitis; reduce throwing and refer.
How is it different from lateral elbow tendinopathy? Pain on resisted wrist flexion and pronation rather than extension.

fields.Position and action: Elbow extended, forearm supinated; patient flexes and pronates against resistance

tests.name: Passive wrist extension with elbow extended and forearm supinated

fields.Position and action: Elbow flexed 20 to 30 degrees; stabilise the humerus; apply outward force at the forearm
Shoulder abducted, elbow fully flexed; apply valgus and quickly extend the elbow
fields.Meaning: UCL injury in throwers [Ref – to verify]

redFlags.Finding: Trauma with deformity or inability to move

manualNotes: Education and load management as for lateral elbow tendinopathy (Vol 6 Ch 1).
Exercise: isometric wrist flexion and pronation, then slow heavy wrist flexor, pronator and grip strengthening, then sport-specific loading (golf swing, throwing progressions).
Manual therapy: optional soft-tissue work and elbow mobilisation for short-term comfort; ulnar nerve sliders if nerve signs.
Avoid repeated corticosteroid injections near the ulnar nerve and tendon [Ref – to verify].
